messages:
Maya Chen: quick brain dump — I'm sketching a fallback circuit for private control plane traffic when per-customer peering drops. goal: keep control plane availability w/o forcing customers to open broad egress. thinking: connector agent + direct peering primary, ephemeral regional relay as fallback. :thinking:
Alex Ruiz: can you clarify TLS termination? who terminates certs on the relay path? we can't have relays that pierce customer mTLS.
Maya Chen: agree — relay must be mTLS to the connector agent or use double-TLS (client->relay mTLS, relay->controlplane mTLS) and no termination of app certs. relays only proxy TCP/TLS, no termination.
Timothy Park: central relay increases blast radius and costs for traffic egress. we should consider per-region relay pools with per-tenant ACLs so we can shard and rate-limit. also AWS peering quotas are finite.
Sara Lasker: latency SLOs: fallback path will add ~20–80ms depending on region. we need a canary/percent rollout policy so critical customers aren't accidentally routed to fallback often. maybe a health score + failover threshold.
Maya Chen: yep — plan is health score on peering + sustained error threshold (e.g., 5m of conn failures) before switching. fallback should be sticky for a short window (2m) to avoid flip-flopping.
Alex Ruiz: what about source IP preservation? customers want preserved IPs for audit logs and firewalling. relays will NAT by default unless we implement X-Forwarded-For style headers, but that doesn't help customer egress ACLs.
Maya Chen: preserving source IP through a relay is hard (hairpin / proxying). two options: 1) try to preserve using GRE/VXLAN overlay (complex), 2) accept SNAT and emit an identity mapping table for logs (audit-friendly). leaning towards (2) for initial rollout.
Timothy Park: +1 for mapping table. overlay tunnels add operational complexity and break with some vendor firewalls. also need rotation plan for relay IPs — they must be stable enough for customers to whitelist if required.
Sara Lasker: is there a config sketch? i threw something together for discussion:
```yaml
fallback_policy:
  primary: peering
  fallback: relay
  relay:
    mode: regional_pool
    regions: ["us-west-2", "eu-west-1"]
    preserve_source_ip: false
    auth: mTLS
    sticky_window_secs: 120
  thresholds:
    conn_failure_window_secs: 300
    failure_ratio: 0.05
```
Alex Ruiz: that looks reasonable. couple asks: - need per-tenant ACLs on relay nodes - need audit mapping (relay-ip -> source-ip) streamed to logging pipeline - fast rollbacks for misroutes (api to force route back to peering)
Maya Chen: noted. runtime implications: relay nodes must be autoscaled and taggable by tenant. auth via mTLS + token scoping for tenant isolation. logging: we can emit mapping as structured logs to kinesis/stream.
devx-bot: link to previous RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/228-fallback-circuit (summarizes relay vs connector options).
Timothy Park: question re: connector agent behavior when peering is flapping: should agent keep trying peering if control plane says fall back, or should agent respect a central decision? we don't want thrash.
Maya Chen: central decision with backoff. agent reports local health + peering metrics; control plane computes score and issues route command. agent enforces sticky_window_secs.
Sara Lasker: can we add a canary tag so we route only 1% of traffic to relay for 24h and check error budgets?
Maya Chen: yes — rollout plan: canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100 with monitoring. create an alert for error budget delta > 0.5%/hour.
Alex Ruiz: ops note: need playbook for customer support — if a tenant reports IP-allowlist block, we should be able to enumerate mapping and provide relay egress IPs or immediate switch back to peering for that tenant.
ops-bot: deployment scheduled: relay-pool/provisioning -> started (CI #4321).
Maya Chen: next steps I propose:
- spike: implement small regional relay prototype w/ mapping logs (2w)
- infra: define ACL model + stable egress IP pinning options (config knob)
- security review: mTLS double-proxy model + cert rotation implications
- docs: support playbook + rollback API
I can own the spike. volunteers for review? :eyes:
Alex Ruiz: I can review the spike design and help with cert rotation bits.
Timothy Park: will help size relay pool and cost model.
Sara Lasker: i'll add SLO checks and the canary automation in the rollout plan.
Maya Chen: great — I'll open GH issues and a short design doc. thanks all. :+1:
